strings.patient_bundles.patient_meryl_spaanna.pa: Meryl Spaanna
“Hospitalization? Wait. Explain the reason and how many days you expect first. I still have work to hand over at Special Section 3... I didn't say I'd go back sick. Don't glare at me yet.”
“All right, I'll stay in the hospital. I'll hand the maintenance work over to my colleagues. I'll follow your lead on treatment, but tell me promptly if anything changes.”
“Stop! That isn't the procedure we just checked. Is the chart wrong, or has the plan changed? Confirm it first. Don't be vague!”
“Now I understand. If there's a reason for each step, I can cooperate... I'm not trying to find fault. I just don't like missing important checks.”
“You think saying 'follow the procedure' counts as an explanation? I'm not asking for a whole textbook. At least tell me what you're doing next!”
“I can see how seriously you've prepared... You're being thorough. Don't worry, I won't cause trouble on purpose. I may sound tough, but my heart is racing like crazy.”
“General anesthesia... Then I won't even have a chance to ask a question afterward. All right, I'll leave it to you. Tell me the result straight away when I wake up.”
“Epidural anesthesia... I'll be awake, but unable to move my legs? I understand the explanation, but when it's my own body, I still don't like that feeling.”
“Local anesthesia, right? Fine. I'll stay still as instructed. If the pulling inside is uncomfortable, I'll tell you. Don't assume I'm just finding fault.”
“No anesthesia at all?! Wait, have you thought this through? Just telling me to 'bear with it' doesn't count as a pain-control plan!”
“I don't need you to coax me... No, wait. Nurse, say something to me again. Hearing your voices helps me feel safer.”
“It hurts! I said I'd cooperate, not that I could switch off the pain! Doctor, listen to me first—I really can't take it anymore!”
“Don't suddenly hold me on both sides at once! I know I need to stay steady, but without anesthesia I'll really pull away when it hurts... Tell me how you're going to help first!”
“All right, I'll try to hold steady. But that tug inside made even my shoulders flinch... Don't rush me. I'm trying to regulate my breathing.”
“My legs are so numb they won't do what I tell them... I know you'll keep me in position. Just tell me before moving me, please.”
“Hey! Don't bring that blade down yet...! I'm not angry. I'm genuinely frightened!”
“...You've already started cutting? There's no sharp sting, but the pressure inside is so noticeable... You really are operating on me.”
“Ah—! The outside seems numb, but that tug inside made me shake! Doctor, wait. Let me tell you what I'm feeling here!”
“Aah—!! It hurts! You really cut! S-stop for a moment! I know I mustn't move, but my body won't listen to me!”
“...You've stopped? Phew... Give me a little time. I'm not trying to yell at anyone. It just hurt so much I couldn't even get my words out properly.”
“I know, don't move! ...But don't have two people shouting instructions at me at once. Even my fingers are shaking!”
“We have to continue... All right. Warn me before you do anything. Don't leave me guessing, okay?”
“Yes, I'm listening. Knowing which step you've reached is better than hearing nothing... Thank you for explaining.”
“Don't just stare at me... It's not as though I'm planning to run. ...Never mind, keep watching. It actually helps to know someone's paying attention.”
“Doctor? Why has everyone suddenly gone quiet! ...Don't leave me imagining things. At least tell me it's still going smoothly!”
“It's almost over...? All right, I'm holding you to that. I'm sorry I was so sharp earlier... You've really helped me a lot.”
“All right, breathe at the pace you tell me... Phew... I can hold on. Nurse, don't leave. Remind me once more.”
“...Don't make me talk anymore. I'm really tired. Just tell me softly when you're finally done.”
“An enema?... That's part of the preoperative preparations too? Understood. Explain the steps first. Don't just start without warning.”
“Hey, keep your voice down! I'm not refusing... I just don't want the whole corridor hearing what preparations I'm having.”
“All right, I'll cooperate. But usually I direct equipment maintenance, and today I even have to follow a nurse's instructions for something like this... It's so awkward.”
“No enema needed this time?... Then let's do what's actually necessary. Of course I have no objection.”
“We can skip it? Phew... Fine, I admit I just felt relieved. Don't laugh.”
“Skin preparation extends this far? Wait! I know it's preparation, but at least close the curtain first.”
“It's not that I don't trust you... It's just really hard to stay as composed as usual while lying here having someone else take care of this.”
“Fine, I won't move. Tell me where you'll touch next, so I don't flinch at every little thing.”
“No skin preparation? Understood. If this procedure doesn't need it, don't add an extra step.”
“We can leave this part out?... Good news. I was still wondering how to keep myself from blushing.”
“All my hair has to go inside?... There, is that all right? Don't look at me. I know my hair's a mess.”
“Putting on this cap suddenly makes it feel as though I'm about to enter the operating room... Tch, I really don't feel at ease.”
“Arms here, turn a little... Understood. One person, one step at a time. I'll keep up.”
“Do I really have to hold this position until the operation ends?... Understood. I'll cooperate. Just let me get used to it first.”
“Don't rush to move me this way and that! ...Sorry. Tell me how to position myself and let me try first. If I can't, I'll ask you to help.”
“No anesthesia at all, and you still need to secure me in this position? What happens if the pain makes me pull away!”
“Don't ask me to promise I won't move already... I don't even know how much the next cut will hurt!”
“All right, I'll do my best to hold it. When I really can't bear it, listen to what I'm saying instead of just watching my position.”
“A catheter too?... Understood. I know it's preoperative nursing care. But could you not announce it so loudly in front of everyone!”
“Nurse, tell me before you begin. I'm not questioning you. It's just... Now that I'm the one being cared for, it's rather embarrassing.”
“Ah... W-wait... I'm trying to relax. My mouth can sound tough, but my body isn't cooperating.”
“This preparation is still needed without anesthesia... All right, I know. But please don't touch me without warning. I'm really tense right now.”
“Is this step still not finished?... I'm not complaining that you're slow. Thinking about going straight into the incision afterward is making me panic more.”
“Please let me catch my breath first. Just the catheter has my whole body tensed up. What am I going to do when the incision actually starts...”
“That's cold! ...Oh, it's the antiseptic. Sorry, it just startled me. Go on.”
“You're disinfecting such a large area... Yes, understood. Seeing my own body actually being prepared as an operative field feels strange.”
“Wait, once disinfection is done, you'll be getting ready to cut, right? I'm still completely awake... Are you really going to start like this!”
“That antiseptic is so cold, but all I can think about is the blade coming afterward... No, my heart's racing too fast.”
“I know disinfection itself doesn't hurt, but thinking about the next step makes it impossible to relax.”
“That line is where the incision will be...? All right, I see it. Having it drawn on my own body is much scarier than hearing the explanation.”
“Just tell me before marking it... Mm, it's already done? Doctor, I'm a little afraid to look down now.”
“You're going to cut along this line without anesthesia...? Wait, let me hear the whole explanation first!”
“I was just saying I wouldn't be afraid... But as soon as that mark was drawn, I started wanting to shrink back.”
“Don't bring the blade over yet! ...Sorry, I know it's only the marking so far, but I'm really getting more and more frightened.”
Doctor, I was going to finish the maintenance work I had on hand before coming in, but this is what's happening with my body now: {line}
The most obvious symptom is: {line}. I'm not exaggerating, and there's more to me than losing my temper.
Please record this as well: {line}. I'm used to reporting every anomaly at once so nothing gets missed later.

My name is Meryl Spaanna. I handle machine maintenance and weapons support in VTX Union's Special Section 3. I really hate vagueness at work, and yes, I'm a little impatient... As for that 'Will-o'-the-Wisp' nickname, please don't put it in my medical chart!
strings.patient_bundles.patient_meryl_spaanna.en: “I need to take all my clothes off for this examination? I know it is medically necessary! ...Explain the scope first and close the curtain. I will cooperate.”
“We're leaving this examination for now?... Phew, all right. But don't leave out a necessary examination just to save trouble. I hate that sort of thing.”
“I heard the requirement. You don't have to keep giving orders! ...Fine, I'll do it. Give me a little time first, and close the curtain.”
“...Thank you for explaining first. I'm not actually trying to argue with you. Suddenly having to undergo an examination like this is just rather embarrassing.”
“Don't speak to me in that threatening tone! If there's a medical reason, explain it and I'll cooperate. There's no need to bully me with your attitude.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi, I have handed everything over at Special Section 3. Could you go over today's surgical arrangements again? I do not like finding out at the last moment that something has not been confirmed.”

“I would like the details. From positioning and disinfection to the actual incision, what will you do along the way?... It is not that I enjoy finding fault. When I think about it being done to my own body, I cannot settle for just hearing 'don't worry'.”

At first, Meryl listens with a stern face, as though reviewing a technical report that must be checked. As the medical staff carefully explain the coming incision, retraction, and surgical procedures, she gradually stops asking questions. Hearing that these steps will soon be performed on her own body, she grips the blanket. For the first time, clear fear shows in her previously sharp gaze.
